text: Meet Zana. A place to organize your projects, work with AI agents, and keep everything in view.
Start by adding a project.
Choose a local folder. You can also clone a repository or connect to a remote project.
Now your work has a home.
Create an agent and choose your preferred provider. Here, we'll use Codex.
Describe the outcome you want, along with any constraints. Then send it off.
The agent reads the project and starts making changes. You can follow its activity as it works.
The Agents board gives you an overview across your projects.
When a decision needs your input, the thread moves to Needs you.
Open the question, choose an answer, and let the work continue.
You can inspect the changed files right beside the conversation.
Watch the checks finish, then review the result.
The agent summarizes what changed. Open the preview to see the dashboard it built.
Back on the board, the thread is idle and ready for your next instruction.
With the GUS plugin connected to your account, your tickets are right here.
Choose Me and the current sprint to focus on your own work.
Open a ticket to see its details. Watch it to keep it close.
The conversation and acceptance criteria stay with the ticket.
Work with agent prepares a draft with the ticket context. Review it, then send.
The agent can pick up from the work you're already tracking.
Plugins bring your tools into Zana. And you can create your own.
Describe your idea in plain language. Let's make a Focus Board with daily priorities, checkboxes, and a completion count.
The agent uses the Plugin Guide, builds the panel, and checks its behavior.
You can follow the build just like any other task.
Review the plugin's access, then install and enable it locally.
Your new tool appears in the sidebar, ready to use.
Check off a priority and watch the count update.
Add another task. A small tool, built around your day.
Start a project. Give an agent a goal. Stay in the loop, keep your tickets close, and make Zana your own.
